claim.pdf_says: 10.6.3   General rule -- a third-level subsection of 10.6 COBOL compilation group, printed identically to 10.6.1 General format which precedes it.
claim.markdown_says: ## 10.6.3 General rule -- level 2, the same level as its parent '## 10.6 COBOL compilation group' and above its sibling '### 10.6.1 General format'. ('## 10.6.2  Syntax rules', on page 289, has the same defect.)
claim.why_it_matters: 10.6.3 detaches from 10.6 in the outline, so the general rule for compiling program/function prototype definitions no longer appears under the COBOL compilation group section that scopes it. Consistent with the same defect at 9.3.7/9.3.8 and 9.3.13/9.3.14.

verdict.reasoning: INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED, but the finding is mislabelled and mis-scoped. Rendered spec_p290.png at 300dpi and read it directly; also rendered pp. 286 and 289 to compare the sibling headings' printed form. PDF FACTS: p.286 prints, in the same bold face and the same point size, '10.6 COBOL compilation group' immediately followed by '10.6.1 General format'; p.289 prints '10.6.2 Syntax rules'; p.290 prints '10.6.3 General rule'. All four are typographically identical run-in bold subclause headings, so the PDF conveys depth solely through the ISO dot-count numbering, which places 10.6.1/10.6.2/10.6.3 one level below 10.6. MARKDOWN FACTS (specs/ISO_COBOL.md): line 12439 '## 10.6 COBOL compilation group', line 12442 '### 10.6.1 General format', line 12641 '## 10.6.2 Syntax rules', line 12675 '## 10.6.3 General rule'. So 10.6.3 is encoded at the SAME markdown level as its own parent 10.6 while its sibling 10.6.1 sits a level deeper -- the transcription is self-inconsistent inside one clause, and any outline/TOC derived from heading depth pops 10.6.3 out of 10.6. The transcription's own dominant convention is level 3 for x.y.z (immediately adjacent 10.7 is transcribed correctly: '## 10.7 End markers' with '### 10.7.1 General', '### 10.7.2 General format', '### 10.7.3 Syntax rules', '### 10.7.4 General rule'), which rules out a deliberate flattening policy. REFUTATION CHECKS ALL FAILED TO REFUTE: the heading is not reflowed onto an adjacent line, is not page-break furniture, is not a wrap/hyphenation artifact, and the claim misquotes neither source (both quoted strings, including the double space in '## 10.6.2 Syntax rules', are byte-exact). WHAT THE CLAIM GETS WRONG: (a) 'missing-heading' is a misnomer -- nothing is missing; the heading text '10.6.3 General rule' is present and verbatim correct, as is every other glyph on the page (items 2)-5), sub-items a)-f), and the single general rule 1) all transcribe verbatim, including 'as specified in 8.13, External repository'). This is a wrong-heading-LEVEL defect, not a lost heading. (b) It is not a page-290 issue. It is one instance of a systematic transcription defect: 276 of the 784 x.y.z-numbered headings in specs/ISO_COBOL.md are emitted at level 2 instead of level 3 (508 are correct), i.e. ~35% of all third-level subclauses, starting as early as 4.2.5 on line 2418. (c) No normative text, section number, or anchor is lost -- '' precedes the heading, so anchor-based cross-references and any citation of 10.6.3 still resolve; the impact is confined to heading-depth-derived outlines/navigation. Verdict real=true because the encoded hierarchy genuinely differs from what the PDF's numbering conveys and the transcription contradicts itself within clause 10.6, but this must be ledgered once as a document-wide heading-level normalization pass, not 276 times as per-page findings.
verdict.corrected_description: kind should be wrong-heading-level (not missing-heading); severity structural, non-normative. The heading text is present and verbatim: PDF p.290 prints '10.6.3 General rule' in the identical bold subclause style used for '10.6.1 General format' (p.286) and '10.6.2 Syntax rules' (p.289), and the markdown carries the same words plus a correct '' anchor. The defect is the markdown heading DEPTH: line 12675 emits '## 10.6.3 General rule' at level 2, equal to its own parent '## 10.6 COBOL compilation group' (line 12439) and shallower than its sibling '### 10.6.1 General format' (line 12442), so heading-depth-derived outlines lift 10.6.3 (and 10.6.2, line 12641) out of the clause that scopes them. No spec text, numbering, or anchor is lost, so no citation of 10.6.3 is impaired. This is NOT a page-local finding: 276 of 784 x.y.z headings across specs/ISO_COBOL.md (~35%, earliest at 4.2.5, line 2418) carry the same level-2/level-3 error, while the immediately following clause 10.7 is transcribed correctly (### for 10.7.1-10.7.4), confirming level 3 is the intended convention. Fix as a single global normalization pass that re-levels every x.y.z heading to '###' (and audits deeper x.y.z.w headings likewise), not as 276 individual page repairs.
